entry.title: Good For Something
entry.summary: I gotta tell you. This old(ish) curmudgeon gimmick is hard. Putting…
entry.content:
I gotta tell you.

This old(ish) curmudgeon gimmick is hard.

Putting on the grimaced furrow and constant outrage.

Because the truth is, I am pretty (and) happy.

And it's hard to be pretty (and) happy and still swing your fists at the sun.

I mean I do it, but it's hard.

Middle-aged and crazy.

I got the whole world figured out, you know.

And my conclusion is:

I choose not to run!

Now, if you're one of those "change the world" types, you might view this as a weakness.

And that's fine.

That's fine.

I gave up caring when I starting writing on the internet.

And I started that a long, long time ago.

In this galaxy.

Although to be fair, I stopped for years at times because I did care.

For moments.

For seasons.

But alas, near death survival gives you a something of a IDGAF attitude.

I call it gratitude.

I already sorta had that.

So it just stacked.

One on top of the other.

Stacking IDGAFs.

Highly recommend.

Within reason.

I always thought I was somewhat of a chaotic good lawyer, which, by definition, is probably not ideal.

Shoutout to my DND nerds.

It just sounds funny.

Chaotic good lawyer.

Makes me chuckle.

But if I'm honest, I'm probably neutral good.

A terrible name.

But it's what they call it.

I'm no longer practicing law, so I'm a neutral good something.

Just not sure what.

You know, we all shoot for great.

Strive for it, even.

But good's better.

Always has been, always will be.

Good's best.

Because you see, they're not on the same scale.

At least, not the way I see it.

Good isn't below great because they're not measuring the same thing.

I'm talking alignment good.

Not Jim Collins good.

Great to Good.

You might not see it yet, but if you do, if you do.

The world is yours.

Here.

🌏

Take it.

Just leave me a little slice.

🍕

For me and my tribe.

Somewhere by the water.

So I can cool the fire.

Be good, greatness.

"Have fun storming the castle!"

"Think it'll work?"

"It would take a miracle."

🏯

entry.title: Autumnal
entry.summary: You would think, I think, that I wouldn't forget to do…
entry.content:
You would think, I think, that I wouldn't forget to do something I do (almost) everyday.

But I do.

I forget.

In my defense, I thought I already wrote today.

But I guess I didn't.

Hey, it happens.

I've been thinking a lot.

As much as I do.

About things that used to be made better.

It never was an outright topic, but it's been coming up in my brain.

Vehicles.

I don't want a touch screen to turn on the heat.

Baseball cards.

Vintage and 90s parallels.

Video games.

You used to be able to own them in physical form.

I don't know if it's nostalgic me.

Autumn does that you know.

Wakes up nostalgic me.

I'm up, I'm up! 

I suppose I never sound older then when I talk about the good old days.

And the truth is, as good as they were, I love now more than ever.

More than yesterdays.

This whole evolution thing is a lot for an old(ish) man.

Cars drive themselves.

Kinda cool.

Big bucks are entrenched in cardboard.

It's an alternative asset class!!!

And every dang thing is a subscription or freemium.

You can play for free, but if you want to be cool, you have to pay.

A lot.

Did you know that they used to sell audiobooks on CD?

What's a CD? Cowboys wide receiver?

Ahh, football season.

They give these college kids millions now!

Over the table instead of under!

NIL.

I think I got a couple years eligibility left.

Go deep! 

🏃

[Closes door after you run through it].

🚪

Tee hee, works every time.

Arm does feel pretty good, though.

entry.title: Do Make Be
entry.summary: "I have a question for you...No. I got something to say:…
entry.content:
"I have a question for you...No.

I got something to say:

I'm going to do something with my life.

Yeah, man."

"Good!"

"Dude, I got these ideas  - I got so many ideas burning through my skull, buddy."

Ever think about what it means to do something with your life?

To make something of yourself?

To be somebody?

What's that mean, anyways?

How does one measure it?

How do you?

I'm going to tell you something.

This idea of doing something with, making something of, and being somebody is a big part of iterating.

But not in the ways you might think.

You see, when most folks talk about do make be, it's usually tinted by the lens of others.

What's acceptable, time-honored, and all that bull sheet.

I'm here to tell you, I've done a lot of this the wrong way.

Be do make.

Have I done something with my life?

Made something of myself?

Do I be somebody?

Maybe not to you.

But I think so.

I think so.

And I believe that's all that matters.

What do you think?

Ah, do whatever you want (within reason).

Make it all up as you go along.

Works for me.

Be all that you can be (in the military or civilian).

What the heck else are you going to do with your time?

Read a friggin' blog musings column?

entry.title: Grandmaster Of None
entry.summary: I ain't grand yet. But I'd like to be. Some day.
entry.content:
I ain't grand yet.

But I'd like to be.

Some day.

In the distant future.

Now, I ain't talking my kids having kids.

Way too early.

Way.

I'm talking about mastery.

Grandmastery.

I've always wanted to be a grandmaster.

You know, the wise, eccentric, curmudgeony, old dude, with arguably superhuman abilities.

I'm getting up there in age.

What a blessing.

Not grandmastery age, but closer than I've ever been.

Almost seeing it, out on the horizon.

Age wise, if not in ability.

Now, I got a confession to make.

I ain't going to be grandmastery age without being a grandmaster.

In something.

That sheet don't compute.

And since you can't be a grandmaster of all trades, what shall I be grandmaster of?

That's a fine question, if not a bit pompous.

But that's what I do.

Ask fine, pompous, questions of myself.

I hope you all can guess by now I'm always half-joking.

Except when I'm not.

50/50.

But there's always some truth there.

Even I have to admit it.

I try to be me, here.

The real me.

Toned down.

I couldn't give you real me, that I think would be bad for everyone.

Grandmaster of musings columns?

No, no, that sounds awful.

Just awful.

Grandmaster of grandmasters?

Great-grandmaster?

Oh, no.

That just sounds old.

No ish about it.

Pretty bad arse, though.

The wonderful thing about grandmastery, I think, is that there's always time to figure it all out.

Thank You for the time.

Maybe I can be one of those martial arts grandmasters that flick two fingers at a charging student and flip him over a little too choreographically.

Grandmaster Chung.

Hey, gotta ring to it.

🥋

Now, where did I put that how to five point palm book?

Oh right, sold it to Pai.

If I'm honest, though, I'm probably striving for grandjack of all trades.

A grand-dilletante.

A grand-dilly.

And I'm ok with that.

I mean, it's still got "grand" in it.

And that's what I'm going for, you know.

The grand part.

🎹

entry.title: If You Can't Spot The Sucker
entry.summary: I've been wrestling with this idea. More a musing. And sure,…
entry.content:
I've been wrestling with this idea.

More a musing.

And sure, it's dropped some elbows on me.

But I kicked out, brother.

Rising up shaking...

As a young(ish) old(ish) Korean(ish) American man, I gamble.

👈

You!!!

Or at least, I used to.

I did it until the point where I understood I no longer watched the game because of the game, but because of the wager.

The bet became the game.

And it's that way right now, for a lot of us.

The game is coated with the filter of your wager.

Sports have become synonymous with gambling.

Sports = gambling.

And here's the crazy part:

Gambling is now becoming synonymous with investing.

Gambling = investing.

Prediction markets and sportsbooks are creeping into people's investing dollars.

Folks are using hard-earned savings to gamble.

Doing more than that.

And some of these apps now have odds on current events right next to your retirement accounts.

Will Alex say a cuss word in his weird, cleanish, way in this musing?

That's the goal, you know.

To create an all-in-one "super" app where you can bank, invest, gamble, predict, and (hopefully still) retire.

There's this old advertising line where if something is different, make it familiar. And if something is familiar, make it different.

Sports is now gambling.

Once taboo.

Now accepted.

No, encouraged and sponsored by.

That's different.

Gambling is now part of people's investment plan.

That's familiar.

And this usually happens in times of desperation.

For those who are struggling to make any headway.

And it got me reeling:

Is this the new American Dream?

1...

To hit some sort of huge win through one of these mechanisms?

2...

It makes a ton of sense that in this age, a lot of our addictions are digital.

...He kicked out!...

But the impacts are very visceral.

Very analog.

We got casinos in our pockets now.

Banks, too.

That's too close to begin with.

But now, they're in the same app.

Right next to our dreams.

They're in the app now, too.

📲

There's a fortune to be made for the fortune tellers.

Always has been.

Always will.

But that don't apply to the one asking.

Never has.

Never will.

Now, I'm a bettor.

In a different way, but familiar.

I make asymmetric bets.

Small ins, big outs.

But this just seems crazy.

Calling gambling a legit form of investment.

But it do sound familiar.

Sheet.

We have a winner!

💰

Something ain't right.

Got a hunch.

100:1?

Yawn.

1T:1?

I'm listening.

entry.title: Must Have Versus Nice To Have
entry.summary: Unlimited wants. Limited needs. Ever hear that? It's this idea that…
entry.content:
Unlimited wants.

Limited needs.

Ever hear that?

It's this idea that you really only need a few things.

But you want everything.

Or at least, that's the theory.

And that the less you truly need, the better.

And so you ask yourself, "Self, do I want this or do I need this?"

If the subject is oxygen, the answer is need.

If the subject is another product made by the fruit company, the answer is want.

Sometimes, needs feel like wants and wants feel like needs.

So what do you want that feels like a need?

And, more importantly, what is a need that feels like a want?

You will find that the wants stack is voluminous.

Encyclopedic.

And that the needs stack is a pretty quick read.

A musings column.

I want you to understand the difference.

You need to.

entry.title: No Wizards
entry.summary: Do you want the truth or do you want the hope?…
entry.content:
Do you want the truth or do you want the hope?

Truth is we all got a finite timeline.

Walking this earth.

A begin date.

And a date with destiny.

Everything in between is life.

The hope is, then, that there's something that turns on when the lights go out.

That's the truth.

That's the hope.

The truth is, most folk don't want it.

The truth that is.

They think they do, but they really want the hope.

Truth is often nasty.

"You can't handle the truth!"

Dirty.

Filthy.

Horrific beyond conceivability.

"There are some books that are never meant to be read."

But truth can also be wondrous.

Magical.

The best beyond all belief.

Wuv. True wuv.

And that's the truth most want.

I hope.

And so, truth seekers, seek more hope.

And hope seekers, well, keep doing your thing.

The people who seek truth wear it on their flesh.

It's broken them, if they've sought it long enough.

But those who seek hope, glow.

The longer they've done it, the deeper the radiance.

I've turned more hope into truth, I still can't believe it.

It don't even make sense looking back.

I think I glow.

That's just the radiation and platinum in your body.

☢

That sheet just gave me a superpower.

Mutated to thankful.

Grateful.

Humble(ish).

So pay no attention to the man behind the curtain.

He's doing atrocious things to keep the world churning.

Same as it ever was.

Embrace the road.

Gold-bricked.

Ruby slippered.

With your people.

Follow it, and it will take you home.

Fowo you foeva.

I hope.

Hey, would you look at that.

You've had it with you all along.

👠

That's the gospel truth.

Click.

Click.

Boom.

Click.

"You used to be fun. You used to be warped and twisted and hilarious... and I mean that in the best way. I mean it as a compliment!"
"I was hilarious once, wasn't I?

entry.title: Thumbs Up
entry.summary: AI is moving fast. AI fast. The Answer! Remember when ai…
entry.content:
AI is moving fast.

AI fast.

The Answer!

Remember when ai couldn't do text in images?

Spelling things wrong in pictures.

So many six-fingered people Inigo looking at all of them funny.

It's flawless, now.

Somewhat.

What's staggering to me is how fast it's getting better.

And I'm not even on the cusp of this sheet.

I just play around with it when I want to.

And it's just noticeably better each time I pick it up.

Couldn't do that before.

Just bewildering what it can do with a little nudge.

I don't prompt.

I nudge.

[Nudging].

Now, with agents, you don't even have to be there.

I haven't gone that deep.

I want to be there.

I don't trust humans.

You think I'm going trust compute with a mission?

At the rate it's going though.

How soon before you trust it over humans.

How soon before it's better than most humans.

Uhh...

Are we already there?

It's already pretty fast.

Reliable.

Does good work.

Does it hallucinate?

Sure, who doesn't?

But it's less than it did before.

It's getting better.

After every iteration.

When the folks at the forefront of this literal machine are demanding we slow the eff down with all this running towards _______, it makes you wonder.

What are they seeing that we don't get to?

Bah.

I'm probably overreacting.

Like I am wont to do.

Underreact 99% of time.

Overreact 1%.

You mostly see the latter.

It's changing so fast.

We need to feed it more.

More compute now.

It's ravenous.

But, on the flip side, when I ask it something, it tells me.

No lip.

No delay (a few seconds).

And a good answer.

We're doomed.

Aww sheet.

Seen this movie before, y'all.

👍

Week one.

Their dad.

entry.title: Emergent
entry.summary: Psst. Hey you. Who me? Yeah. Get over here. Now, the…
entry.content:
Psst.

Hey you.

Who me?

Yeah.

Get over here.

Now, the first thing I gotta tell you is.

Never approach someone who "pssts" you.

But now that you're here, let's talk.

25 years ago, yesterday, something big happened.

What came with it was a lot of ugly.

A ton of it.

Foogly amounts.

The whole country shut down.

Sounds familiar.

In a bit of a haze.

I remember even sports shut down.

Hmm.

And when it finally reopened, I went to a Giants game.

They warned us to stay home.

Be safe.

It was the first since all of it happened.

And in the air was this mix of anger and patriotism.

A country united in rage.

People who looked a certain way wore red, white, and blue.

And people who looked another way stayed home.

You could, as Gorilla Monsoon would say:

"Cut the intensity with a knife!"

When the anthem was about to play, it got eerily quiet.

"Please rise."

Unnecessary because everyone was already standing.

You could hear your heartbeat.

"For the playing of our national anthem."

And when the music started, the entire stadium sang from their burals and bits.

Every mother mother in there sang the anthem.

Or so it seemed.

We weren't singing it half-heartedly and half-arsed either.

We sang full-hearted.

Full-arsed.

Only way to sing.

And when it was over.

The roar.

My God, the roar.

Still gives me goosebumps.

Deafening.

The stadium shook.

From the release of pent-up anger, confusion, rage, and pride.

But it was manifested as joy.

As glee.

As jubilance.

Sure, we all wanted blood.

But we would take camaraderie.

We would take celebration to mourn.

And we knew, we just knew, that revenge was coming.

In the form of a 100 foot tall pissed off bald eagle.

Now, looking back, I'm not sure if we got payback.

I'll leave that to you experts in vengeance.

But don't kill the moment.

Quarter century.

So much has changed.

What I choose to remember most, though.

Is a choir of 41,000 singing our nation's anthem.

United.

Through tears and strength.

Through song.

And the roar.

My God.

🇺🇸

Out of the ashes.
